chunks: Ali ibn Atiyyah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
"Fajr is that which, when you see it, appears spread out horizontally, as though it were the whiteness of the River Sūrā."

key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: the true dawn marking the beginning of daybreak
key_terms.نَهَرِ سُورَى: the River Sūrā, used here as a visual comparison

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام describe the true fajr?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the true fajr as the dawn that spreads horizontally across the horizon. It serves as a practical sign for recognizing the beginning of the time connected to worship, especially salat and sawm.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1436 - Ali ibn Atiyyah narrated from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:
"The true Fajr (dawn) is the one that, when you see it, appears spread out horizontally, like the whiteness of the Surā river."
